tick_and_fixed_point.definition: A tick is one character-state update; use integer/Q8.8 position and velocity. Final wall-clock mapping must be specified for NTSC 60Hz and PAL 50Hz.
tick_and_fixed_point.grounded: x[n+1] = x[n] + vx[n]; vx[n+1] approaches target speed with bounded acceleration; reverse direction brakes before changing sign.
tick_and_fixed_point.jump_and_fall: With screen y increasing downward: x[n+1]=x[n]+vx[n], y[n+1]=y[n]+vy[n], vy[n+1]=vy[n]+g. Choose initial vy and g so the arc meets declared apex/landing tick; derive knockback vx from the hit event.
tick_and_fixed_point.lunge: Advance follows bounded acceleration from planted rear foot, then braking from front-foot contact; sum of per-tick displacement equals declared candidate travel.
tick_and_fixed_point.boomerang: Use a deterministic integer/Q8.8 lookup arc: one-way travel 24 ticks to 96px range, 12px apex offset, then 24-tick return on miss. One active object; collision consumes it in this fan-game proposal. These are unmeasured candidate values, not real aerodynamics.

motion_models.balance_method: Compare each move against the same baseline in hit, block and whiff states. Measure startup/active/recovery, damage as a fraction of approved life, pushback, hitstun, resource use and counterplay; tune only after ROM/emulator playtests.
